page: Microsoft Azure FX12mds_v2 is a specialized instance configuration that pairs high-frequency processing with an expansive memory footprint. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system is driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated virtual CPUs across 6 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The CPU architecture includes a generous 260 MB Level 3 cache, 2 MB Level 2 cache per core, and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets, enabling hardware acceleration for integer and bfloat16 matrix operations without dedicated GPUs.

Hardware resource allocation is characterized by an asymmetric ratio of compute to RAM. The instance features 252 GB of system memory, which yields an exceptionally high 21 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed locally through a bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD, providing high-speed ephemeral capacity suitable for heavy scratchpad operations, caching layers, and fast swap space. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, directing compute execution entirely through the host CPU cores and specialized vector extensions.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded execution, placing the instance in the top 10% on Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2,358, accompanied by high throughput in text processing and small-model LLM generation. Compression benchmarks mirror this strength, with single-threaded gzip and bzip3 achieving top-quartile results. However, multi-threaded throughput and raw CPU scores across stress-ng and PassMark settle within the median range, directly bounded by the 6-core physical ceiling.

The primary tradeoff of the FX12mds_v2 lies in its thread-to-memory density. It avoids the core-count bloat common to memory-heavy servers, ensuring high per-core licensing and execution efficiency. This profile makes the instance particularly effective for memory-intensive yet thread-constrained workloads, including electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caching systems, relational database instances requiring large buffer pools, and high-frequency financial modeling.

It incorporates 252 GB of system memory, yielding an uncommonly high 21 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD for fast transient storage. The heavy allocation of memory relative to vCPUs offers strong resource density for workloads requiring high clock speeds alongside large memory footprints, such as in-memory databases, electronic design automation, batch financial modeling, and specialized data engineering pipelines.
